question: Which directive principle was added by the 97th Amendment Act 2011?

options.text: Uniform civil code for the citizens

solution:
The correct answer is __**Promotion of co-operative societies**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Promotion of co-operative societies** was added to the** Directive Principles of State Policy by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011**.
 
• This amendment aims to encourage the development of cooperative societies, which play a significant role in the socio-economic development of the country.
 
• The inclusion of this directive principle underscores the importance of cooperative societies in achieving equitable growth and development.
 
• Cooperative societies are organizations owned and operated by a group of individuals for their mutual benefit, and they cover various sectors including agriculture, banking, and housing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The 97th Amendment Act** was passed by the** Parliament of India in December 2011** and came into effect on **15th February 2012**.
 
• This amendment also made changes to **Part IXB of the Constitution**, which deals with the incorporation, regulation, and winding up of cooperative societies.
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government, and they aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The principles set forth in** Part IV** of the Indian Constitution are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Directive Principles are intended to be used as a yardstick by the government to frame policies and laws aimed at ensuring social and economic democracy.
